text: The conflicting "normal" ultrasound results are concerning given the prior X-ray findings of a distal obstruction. Please tell me: was your baby born prematurely, and do you have any family history of intestinal atresia or Hirschsprung's disease? Also, does the baby pass any gas?

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Distal Intestinal Obstruction (likely Distal Intestinal Obstruction Syndrome or distal atresia) with conflicting imaging results.

The clinical picture of feeding difficulties, abdominal distension, and a prior X-ray showing a distal obstruction with no rectal gas is highly suggestive of a distal obstruction. The "normal" ultrasound results are likely false negatives given the severity of the X-ray findings. Since the baby was born at term without complications and has no fever or diarrhea, this is not an infectious colitis. The absence of meconium passage history and family history further narrows the differential.
